title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps to v81 - BREAKING, an incompatible project-format change.
   v78 is upstream's own step (eserved_tools, #2604), v79 its
   conditional tip form (#3368) and v80 the minimum_cone_radius step
   (#3153); a v78 or v79 reader accepts this branch's old v78 and
   drops the stated key on re-save. v81 is the next correctly-ordered
   free version: an older reader refuses the file rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named. A v78, v79 and v80 file still open - the v79 keys read
   natively, pinned by the round-trip test).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `a_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v81 round-trip, v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin),
  `a_stated_axis_on_every_rotary_kind_needs_the_new_reader` (the
  old-reader boundary, one op of each rotary kind),
  `a_common_translation_does_not_defeat_the_stated_line_judge` (the
  review's mutation: the model and stock at Y+10000, clearance 100 -
  the work offset on the part generates, 1 mm and 2 mm off refuse by
  name).
- motion `axis_stated_tests`, the translation pins: a part moved with
  its line holds it on every coordinate axis and reads the fit's own
  axis; a wrong line 1 mm off on each of the three coordinate planes
  refuses at home and after every common translation.
- app `project_roundtrip`:
  `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_project_version` (the ladder
  stepped past v79: a tip-form file writes v81, and a v79 file - the
  tip-form era's own - still opens and reads its tips whole).
- ui `egui_app::tests::rotary_stated_axis` (new, the review's item):
  the group's labels, roles and enabled state, the Apply commit and
  one undo, across the three rotary kinds
  (`the_stated_axis_group_arms_edits_and_undoes_on_every_rotary_kind`);
  the help text follows the resolver's order - the machine's stated
  line first, the fit only when nothing is stated
  (`the_help_text_follows_the_resolver_machine_line_first`).
- Test placement: `crates/app/tests/rotary_stated_axis.rs` stays a
  top-level binary because no existing directory suite covers the
  rotary domain - its siblings (`rotary_verify.rs`,
  `rotary_letter.rs`, `rotary_contour_x.rs`) are all top-level - and
  its gate map spans app::rotary_stated, app::operation, app::project
  and the motion judge.
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v81 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Screenshots

Before and after of the Passes tab's stated-axis controls (the
fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, captured through the
egui_kittest properties-page harness - no pixels enter this branch):

- [before](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-before.png) -
  the pre-change Passes tab, no stated-axis group
- [after, unstated](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-after-unstated.png) -
  the group sits above the passes, disarmed
- [after, stated](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-after-stated.png) -
  armed, the three direction rows seeded with X
- [after, the offset kind](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-offset-after-stated.png) -
  the same group on Rotary Offset's Passes tab

## Not included (the issue stays open)

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing
  (decision part 3/4): the live claim on
  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's
  disagreement refusal keeps the radial kinds locked on helical
  parts until that kernel can consume the stated axis safely.
- No 360-degree radial drop finish for Rotary Parallel, no
  Doosan/Fanuc posting of one - same slice.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read a
stated rotation axis first (the operation's own direction, else the
machine's stated rotary line through the work offset origin), judged
against the model's faces - a part on the stated line cuts the fitted
path unchanged, a part whose faces disagree refuses by name (the
4-axis case named), and nothing stated keeps the fitted axis (v81 project files - a breaking project-format change).

fork synced at v0.25.0

Refs #2772
